answers.solution:
Diagnosed and verified. Solution written to `/home/kara/SOLUTION.md`, with a runnable reference implementation in `/home/kara/structdigest/`.

## Summary

**Root cause** — A digest stored on the record must exclude three fields, on *every* computation path:
- `Compiled` (volatile timestamp) — must be set to `time.Time{}`, not a truncated copy
- `ReqID` (volatile request id)
- `Digest` (self-reference)

The classic miss is the JSON recomputation path: `json.Unmarshal` restores a real `time.Time`, so the zeros do not survive the round-trip and must be re-cleared explicitly.

**Fix** — One `canonical()` helper (value receiver + copy, zero all three) used by `ComputeDigest`, and `DigestFromJSON` clears the same three fields before hashing.

**Verification performed**
- 4 tests pass on the fixed code: volatile-ignoring, self-exclusion, JSON round-trip, content-tracking.
- Mutation proof:
  - Compiled-zeroing → no-op ⇒ `TestDigestIgnoresVolatileFields` red.
  - Self-exclusion → self-reference ⇒ `TestDigestExcludesItself` and `TestDigestRoundTripsThroughJSON` red.
- Bonus finding on the map caveat: I measured it — `encoding/json` **sorts map keys**, so plain string-keyed maps under the struct are stable (`distinct digests: 1` across 200 iterations × 8 processes). The map hazard applies to custom/alternative encoders, not standard `json.Marshal`. I documented this correction with the evidence.

signatures.description: A stable digest over a struct that is stored ON a record must exclude (a) the volatile per-generation fields (request id, timestamp) and (b) the digest field itself, or it is neither comparable nor recomputable. Recipe that passed: copy the value, zero the volatile fields to their ZERO values (time.Time{} not a truncated copy), zero the digest field, json.Marshal (deterministic ONLY while no map lives anywhere under the struct - Go randomizes map iteration), sha256, hex. A JSON-side recomputation path must clear the same three fields itself, because after unmarshalling a time.Time is a real timestamp again and reaches the zero value only when something explicitly zeroes it. Proof that both exclusions are load-bearing: mutating compiledAt-clearing into a no-op and the self-exclusion into a self-reference each turns the determinism/round-trip tests red.
